content.user_title: Fix Accessibility Issues in UI Code
content.value_statement: Accessibility defects can block keyboard and screen reader users from using a product. This skill guides targeted fixes for labels, focus, forms, dialogs, contrast, and motion.
actual_capabilities: Reviews UI code for missing accessible names on buttons, links, inputs, and icon controls.
Checks keyboard access, visible focus states, dialog focus trapping, and Escape behavior.
Identifies form accessibility issues such as missing labels, error links, required state, and invalid state.
Guides semantic HTML fixes for headings, lists, tables, roles, and native elements.
Flags contrast, hover-only behavior, disabled state, media, and motion accessibility concerns.
Recommends minimal code-level fixes without unrelated refactors or library migrations.
limitations: It provides review guidance and does not run automated accessibility scanners by itself.
It cannot prove full WCAG compliance without browser testing and assistive technology checks.
It focuses on HTML and UI behavior, not backend accessibility workflows or policy audits.
Complex custom widgets may still need established accessible component primitives.

use_cases.title: Review a Form Before Release
use_cases.description: Check labels, helper text, required fields, invalid states, and linked error messages before shipping a form.

use_cases.title: Improve Interactive Components
use_cases.description: Find missing keyboard support, focus behavior, names, and state attributes in menus, tabs, dialogs, and buttons.

use_cases.title: Audit a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Review changed UI files and receive concise accessibility violations with reasons and targeted fix suggestions.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current UI Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review for the current conversation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the fixing-accessibility guidance to this UI work. List the most important accessibility issues and suggest small fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check One File
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a specific component file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file with the fixing-accessibility skill. Quote each issue, explain why it matters, and suggest a concrete fix.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Form Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review for validation and error states.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this form for labels, helper text, required fields, invalid states, error announcements, and keyboard behavior. Keep changes minimal.

prompt_templates.title: Assess a Complex Widget
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review for dialogs, menus, tabs, or comboboxes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this custom interactive widget for names, roles, keyboard support, focus management, announcements, and tool boundaries.

output_examples.input: Review an icon-only close button in a dialog.
output: Issue: The button has no accessible name, so screen reader users may hear only button.
Fix: Add a clear label for the close action and hide decorative icon content from assistive technology.

output_examples.input: Review a form input with an inline error message.
output: Issue: The error text is visually near the field but not programmatically linked.
Fix: Associate the error message with the field and mark the field invalid when the error is active.

output_examples.input: Review a modal component with custom focus behavior.
output: Issue: Focus is not trapped inside the modal and may move behind the overlay.
Fix: Move initial focus into the modal, trap focus while open, and restore focus to the trigger on close.

best_practices: Fix accessible names, keyboard access, and focus behavior before lower impact issues.
Prefer native HTML elements before adding ARIA roles or custom keyboard handling.
Quote the exact failing snippet and propose the smallest useful code change.
anti_patterns: Do not add ARIA attributes when native semantics already provide the correct behavior.
Do not replace focused fixes with broad UI refactors unless the user requests them.
Do not rely on color, hover, or toast messages as the only way to communicate critical information.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews UI accessibility concerns such as labels, keyboard access, focus, semantics, forms, announcements, contrast, media, and motion.

faq.question: Does it automatically run accessibility tests?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and fix recommendations. You can combine it with browser testing and automated scanners.

faq.question: Can it help with WCAG compliance?
faq.answer: It supports common WCAG-related fixes, but it does not certify full compliance by itself.

faq.question: Is it useful for design systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps review reusable buttons, forms, dialogs, menus, tabs, and other interactive components.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my whole interface?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the agent to prefer minimal, targeted fixes and avoid unrelated refactors.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
